tools.name: FastQC
tools.description: Quality report for raw sequencing reads.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Reads
inputs.description: One or more FASTQ files (plain or .gz). Each gets its own report.

outputs.name: report_dir
outputs.label: Report folder
outputs.description: FastQC writes one HTML report and one zip per input file here.

tools.name: MultiQC
tools.description: Combines the reports of many tools into one HTML page.

inputs.name: reports
inputs.label: Reports to combine
inputs.description: Any results MultiQC understands: FastQC, fastp, Cutadapt, samtools, STAR, HISAT2, Salmon, kallisto, featureCounts, RSeQC. Connect as many steps as you like.

outputs.name: report_dir
outputs.label: Report folder
outputs.description: Folder for the combined report and its data.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Combined report
outputs.description: The HTML page. It is always called multiqc_report.html inside the report folder.

tools.name: mosdepth
tools.description: Fast coverage summary: the average depth per chromosome and in windows along the genome.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM sorted by genome position.

inputs.name: bai
inputs.label: BAM index
inputs.description: The .bai file of this BAM (make it with samtools index). It must sit next to the BAM and be named like it, ending in .bam.bai.

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Coverage folder
outputs.description: Folder for the coverage tables.

outputs.name: summary
outputs.label: Coverage summary
outputs.description: Length, total bases and mean depth of each chromosome. MultiQC reads it.

outputs.name: global_dist
outputs.label: Depth distribution
outputs.description: What fraction of the genome is covered at least N times. MultiQC reads it.

outputs.name: regions
outputs.label: Depth in windows
outputs.description: Mean depth of each window along the genome (compressed BED).

params.label: Window size
params.description: Mean depth is reported for windows of this many bases.

params.label: Minimum mapping quality
params.description: Reads below this mapping quality are not counted.

tools.name: Qualimap BamQC
tools.description: Quality report of an alignment: coverage, mapping quality, insert size and base content.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM sorted by genome position.

outputs.name: report_dir
outputs.label: Report folder
outputs.description: Folder with the HTML report and its data.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Report page
outputs.description: The HTML report. It is always called qualimapReport.html inside the report folder.

outputs.name: results
outputs.label: Summary numbers
outputs.description: The key numbers as text. MultiQC reads it.

params.label: Ignore reads marked as duplicates
params.description: Run MarkDuplicates first, then tick this to leave PCR duplicates out of the numbers.

params.label: Memory limit
params.description: For example 2G or 8G.

tools.name: fastp
tools.description: Fast adapter and quality trimming for FASTQ reads.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Reads
inputs.description: Sequencing reads in FASTQ format (plain or .gz).

outputs.name: trimmed
outputs.label: Trimmed reads
outputs.description: Reads after trimming and filtering.

outputs.name: html_report
outputs.label: HTML report
outputs.description: Before and after statistics, for people.

outputs.name: json_report
outputs.label: JSON report
outputs.description: The same statistics for MultiQC.

params.label: Minimum base quality
params.description: Bases below this Phred quality count as unqualified.

params.label: Minimum read length
params.description: Reads shorter than this after trimming are dropped.

tools.name: Cutadapt
tools.description: Removes adapter sequences and low-quality ends from reads.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Reads
inputs.description: Sequencing reads in FASTQ format (plain or .gz).

outputs.name: trimmed
outputs.label: Trimmed reads
outputs.description: Reads after adapter removal.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Trimming report
outputs.description: Cutadapt's summary of what it removed. MultiQC reads it.

params.label: 3' adapter sequence
params.description: Adapter to cut from the 3' end. The default is the Illumina universal adapter.

params.label: Minimum read length
params.description: Reads shorter than this after trimming are discarded.

params.label: Quality cutoff
params.description: Trim low-quality bases from the 3' end below this Phred score.

tools.name: BWA index
tools.description: Builds the index BWA MEM needs to align reads to a genome.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The genome FASTA to index.

outputs.name: index_dir
outputs.label: Index folder
outputs.description: A copy of the FASTA with the BWA index files next to it.

outputs.name: indexed_ref
outputs.label: Indexed reference
outputs.description: The FASTA copy inside the folder. Connect it to BWA MEM as the reference genome.

tools.name: Bowtie2 build
tools.description: Builds the genome index Bowtie2 needs to align reads.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The genome FASTA to index.

outputs.name: index_dir
outputs.label: Index folder
outputs.description: A copy of the FASTA with the Bowtie2 index files next to it.

outputs.name: index
outputs.label: Genome index
outputs.description: The index name Bowtie2 reads (the FASTA copy inside the folder). Connect it to Bowtie2.

params.label: Genome is larger than 4 billion bases
params.description: Builds the large kind of index. Bowtie2 chooses by itself for most genomes; tick this only if the build asks for it.

tools.name: samtools faidx
tools.description: Indexes a reference FASTA (makes the .fai file variant callers need).

inputs.name: ref
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The genome FASTA to index.

outputs.name: ref_dir
outputs.label: Indexed reference folder
outputs.description: A copy of the FASTA with its .fai index next to it.

outputs.name: fasta
outputs.label: Indexed reference
outputs.description: The FASTA copy inside the folder. Connect it to a variant caller or aligner as the reference genome.

outputs.name: fai
outputs.label: FASTA index
outputs.description: The .fai file that sits next to the FASTA copy.

tools.name: GATK CreateSequenceDictionary
tools.description: Makes the sequence dictionary (.dict) that GATK needs next to the reference.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.label: Reference genome (indexed)
inputs.description: A FASTA that already has its .fai index next to it. Use the output of samtools faidx.

outputs.name: ref_dir
outputs.label: GATK reference folder
outputs.description: A copy of the FASTA with its .fai index and the new .dict file.

outputs.name: fasta
outputs.label: GATK-ready reference
outputs.description: The FASTA copy inside the folder. Connect it to HaplotypeCaller as the reference genome.

outputs.name: fai
outputs.label: FASTA index
outputs.description: The .fai file next to the FASTA copy.

outputs.name: dict
outputs.label: Sequence dictionary
outputs.description: The .dict file next to the FASTA copy.

tools.name: BWA MEM
tools.description: Aligns reads to a reference genome. Writes SAM.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The reference FASTA the reads are aligned to. Connect BWA index to use its indexed copy, or give a FASTA you indexed yourself (the index files sit next to it).

inputs.name: reads1
inputs.label: Reads (first of the pair)
inputs.description: FASTQ with the reads, or the first file of a pair.

inputs.name: reads2
inputs.label: Reads (second of the pair)
inputs.description: Leave empty for single-end reads.

outputs.name: sam
outputs.label: Alignments
outputs.description: The alignments in SAM format.

params.label: Mark shorter split hits as secondary
params.description: Needed by Picard and GATK.

params.label: Minimum seed length
params.description: Matches shorter than this are dropped. Smaller is more sensitive and slower.

tools.name: Bowtie2
tools.description: Aligns single-end reads to an indexed genome. Writes SAM.

inputs.name: index
inputs.label: Genome index
inputs.description: The index made with Bowtie2 build (connect it), or the prefix of one you built yourself: the path without .1.bt2 and the rest.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Reads
inputs.description: Sequencing reads in FASTQ format (plain or .gz).

outputs.name: sam
outputs.label: Alignments
outputs.description: The alignments in SAM format.

params.label: Preset
params.description: Speed against sensitivity.

tools.name: minimap2 (short reads)
tools.description: Aligns short reads (the sr preset) to a reference genome. Writes SAM with a read group.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The genome FASTA the reads are aligned to. No index is needed.

inputs.name: reads1
inputs.label: Reads (first of the pair)
inputs.description: FASTQ with the reads, or the first file of a pair.

inputs.name: reads2
inputs.label: Reads (second of the pair)
inputs.description: Leave empty for single-end reads.

outputs.name: sam
outputs.label: Alignments
outputs.description: The alignments in SAM format.

params.label: Sample name
params.description: Written into every alignment as its read group. GATK and Picard need one. For example patient1.

params.label: Report only the best alignment of each read
params.description: Leaves out the second-best places a read could go. Recommended before variant calling.

tools.name: STAR
tools.description: Splice-aware RNA-seq aligner, single-end or paired-end. Writes a coordinate-sorted BAM.

inputs.name: index
inputs.label: Genome index folder
inputs.description: The folder made with STAR genome index (connect it).

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Reads (first of the pair)
inputs.description: Sequencing reads in FASTQ format (plain or .gz).

inputs.name: reads2
inputs.label: Reads (second of the pair)
inputs.description: Leave empty for single-end reads.

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Output folder
outputs.description: STAR writes the BAM and its logs into this folder.

outputs.name: bam
outputs.label: Alignments
outputs.description: The sorted BAM. It is always called Aligned.sortedByCoord.out.bam inside the output folder.

outputs.name: log
outputs.label: Mapping summary
outputs.description: STAR's mapping statistics. MultiQC reads it.

tools.name: samtools sort
tools.description: Sorts alignments by coordinate (or by read name).

inputs.name: alignments
inputs.label: Alignments
inputs.description: A SAM or BAM file.

outputs.name: bam
outputs.label: Sorted alignments
outputs.description: The sorted BAM.

params.label: Sort by read name
params.description: Off sorts by genome coordinate.

params.label: Memory per thread
params.description: For example 768M or 2G.

tools.name: samtools index
tools.description: Builds the .bai index of a coordinate-sorted BAM.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM file.

outputs.name: bai
outputs.label: BAM index
outputs.description: The .bai file.

tools.name: samtools view
tools.description: Filters alignments and converts them to BAM.

inputs.name: alignments
inputs.label: Alignments
inputs.description: A SAM or BAM file.

outputs.name: filtered
outputs.label: Filtered alignments
outputs.description: The alignments that passed the filters, as BAM.

params.label: Minimum mapping quality
params.description: Alignments below this MAPQ are dropped.

params.label: Keep mapped reads only
params.description: Drops reads that did not align.

tools.name: samtools flagstat
tools.description: Counts reads by alignment flag. Writes a text summary.

inputs.name: alignments
inputs.label: Alignments
inputs.description: A SAM or BAM file.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Summary
outputs.description: Counts of mapped, paired and duplicate reads, as text.

tools.name: samtools merge
tools.description: Combines several sorted BAM files into one.

inputs.name: bams
inputs.label: Alignments
inputs.description: Two or more BAM files sorted the same way. Connect as many steps as you like.

outputs.name: merged
outputs.label: Merged alignments
outputs.description: The combined BAM.

params.label: Inputs are sorted by read name
params.description: Tick this only if the BAM files were sorted by read name. Off means sorted by genome position.

tools.name: samtools markdup
tools.description: Finds PCR duplicates and marks (or removes) them. Runs fixmate and sort first, so plain aligner output works.

inputs.name: alignments
inputs.label: Alignments
inputs.description: A SAM or BAM file with paired-end reads.

outputs.name: marked
outputs.label: Alignments with duplicates marked
outputs.description: A BAM sorted by genome position.

outputs.name: stats
outputs.label: Duplicate statistics
outputs.description: How many reads were examined and how many are duplicates.

params.label: Remove duplicates instead of marking them
params.description: Off keeps every read and only flags the duplicates.

params.label: Optical duplicate distance
params.description: 0 switches optical duplicate detection off. Use 100 for HiSeq-type machines or about 2500 for NovaSeq.

tools.command: set -o pipefail; samtools sort -n -@ {threads} {alignments} | samtools fixmate -m -@ {threads} - - | samtools sort -@ {threads} - | samtools markdup -@ {threads} {remove_duplicates} -d {optical_distance} -f {stats} - {marked}

tools.name: Picard MarkDuplicates
tools.description: Finds PCR duplicates in a sorted BAM and marks (or removes) them. Writes a duplication report.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM sorted by genome position.

outputs.name: marked
outputs.label: Alignments with duplicates marked
outputs.description: The BAM with duplicates flagged.

outputs.name: metrics
outputs.label: Duplication report
outputs.description: How many pairs were examined and how many are duplicates. MultiQC reads it.

params.label: Remove duplicates instead of marking them
params.description: Off keeps every read and only flags the duplicates.

params.label: Optical duplicate distance
params.description: Reads closer than this on the flow cell can be optical duplicates. 100 suits most machines; use 2500 for NovaSeq.

params.label: Memory limit
params.description: For example 2g or 8g.

tools.name: samtools depth
tools.description: Writes how many reads cover each position of the genome, one column per BAM file.

inputs.name: bams
inputs.label: Alignments
inputs.description: One or more BAM files. Each one gets its own column.

outputs.name: depth
outputs.label: Depth table
outputs.description: Columns: chromosome, position, then the depth of each BAM.

params.label: Include positions with no reads
params.description: Off lists only covered positions. On gives one line for every base of the genome, which is a very large file for big genomes.

params.label: Minimum base quality
params.description: Bases below this quality are not counted.

params.label: Minimum mapping quality
params.description: Reads below this mapping quality are not counted.

tools.name: bcftools call
tools.description: Calls SNPs and indels from a sorted BAM (mpileup then call).

inputs.name: ref
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The reference the reads were aligned to. It needs a .fai index: connect the Indexed reference of samtools faidx.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A coordinate-sorted BAM.

outputs.name: vcf
outputs.label: Variants
outputs.description: The called variants in VCF format.

params.label: Minimum mapping quality
params.description: Alignments below this MAPQ are ignored.

tools.command: set -o pipefail; bcftools mpileup --threads {threads} -Ou -f {ref} -q {min_mapq} {bam} | bcftools call --threads {threads} -mv -Ov -o {vcf}

tools.name: FreeBayes
tools.description: Calls SNPs and small indels from one or more sorted, indexed BAM files.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The reference the reads were aligned to. Connect the Indexed reference of samtools faidx to keep the .fai index with it.

inputs.name: bams
inputs.label: Alignments
inputs.description: One or more BAM files, sorted by position. Connect as many steps as you like.

outputs.name: vcf
outputs.label: Variants
outputs.description: The called variants in VCF format.

params.label: Ploidy
params.description: How many copies of each chromosome the sample has: 1 for bacteria, 2 for most animals and plants.

params.label: Minimum fraction of reads with the variant
params.description: A variant is reported only if at least this share of the reads at its position carry it.

params.label: Minimum reads with the variant
params.description: A variant is reported only if at least this many reads carry it.

params.label: Minimum mapping quality
params.description: Reads below this mapping quality are ignored.

params.label: Minimum base quality
params.description: Bases below this quality are ignored.

tools.name: GATK HaplotypeCaller
tools.description: Calls SNPs and small indels by re-assembling the reads around each variant.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.label: Reference genome (GATK-ready)
inputs.description: A FASTA with its .fai and .dict files next to it. Use the output of GATK CreateSequenceDictionary.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM sorted by position whose reads have a read group (minimap2 adds one; for BWA MEM add a sample name).

inputs.name: bai
inputs.label: BAM index
inputs.description: The .bai file of this BAM (make it with samtools index). It must sit next to the BAM and be named like it, ending in .bam.bai.

outputs.name: vcf
outputs.label: Variants
outputs.description: The called variants in VCF format.

params.label: Ploidy
params.description: How many copies of each chromosome the sample has: 1 for bacteria, 2 for most animals and plants.

params.label: Minimum base quality
params.description: Bases below this quality are ignored.

params.label: Minimum confidence to call a variant
params.description: Variants whose confidence score is lower are left out. Higher means stricter.

params.label: Memory limit
params.description: For example 2g or 8g.

tools.name: bcftools filter
tools.description: Keeps the variants that are good enough (enough quality and depth), or marks the others.

inputs.name: vcf
inputs.label: Variants
inputs.description: A VCF file. Every variant needs a depth value (DP), which most callers write.

outputs.name: filtered
outputs.label: Filtered variants
outputs.description: The variants that passed.

params.label: Minimum quality
params.description: Variants with a lower QUAL score fail.

params.label: Minimum depth
params.description: Variants covered by fewer reads fail.

params.label: Mark failing variants instead of removing them
params.description: On keeps every variant and writes LowQuality in its FILTER column. Off removes them.

tools.name: bcftools norm
tools.description: Writes variants in one standard form: indels left-aligned, optionally one line per alternative allele.

inputs.name: vcf
inputs.label: Variants
inputs.description: A VCF file.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The reference the variants were called against.

outputs.name: normalized
outputs.label: Normalized variants
outputs.description: The variants in standard form.

params.label: Split sites with several alternative alleles
params.description: Gives each alternative allele its own line, so downstream tools see simple records.

params.label: Stop if the reference base does not match
params.description: Off only warns when a variant's reference base differs from the genome.

params.label: Remove duplicate lines
params.description: Drops lines that are exactly alike.

tools.name: bcftools stats
tools.description: Counts the variants in a VCF: SNPs, indels, transitions and transversions. MultiQC reads it.

inputs.name: vcf
inputs.label: Variants
inputs.description: A VCF file.

outputs.name: stats
outputs.label: Variant statistics
outputs.description: The counts as text.

params.label: Also count for each sample
params.description: Adds a block of numbers for every sample in the file.

tools.name: bgzip
tools.description: Compresses a VCF, BED or other table so it can be indexed with tabix.

inputs.name: file
inputs.label: File to compress
inputs.description: A plain text VCF, BED, GTF or table.

outputs.name: compressed
outputs.label: Compressed file
outputs.description: The same content, compressed. Name it .vcf.gz for a VCF or .bed.gz for a BED.

params.label: Compression level
params.description: 1 is fastest, 9 gives the smallest file.

tools.name: tabix
tools.description: Indexes a compressed, sorted VCF, BED or GFF so a region can be read without reading the whole file.

inputs.name: file
inputs.label: Compressed file
inputs.description: A sorted file compressed with bgzip.

outputs.name: index_dir
outputs.label: Indexed file folder
outputs.description: A copy of the file with its .tbi index next to it.

outputs.name: indexed
outputs.label: Indexed file
outputs.description: The compressed copy inside the folder.

outputs.name: index
outputs.label: Index
outputs.description: The .tbi file next to the compressed copy.

params.label: File kind
params.description: What the file holds: variants (vcf), regions (bed) or annotation (gff).

tools.name: snpEff build database
tools.description: Builds a snpEff database for your own genome from its FASTA and gene annotation (GTF).

inputs.name: genome
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The genome FASTA.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.description: The genes in GTF format.

outputs.name: database
outputs.label: snpEff database
outputs.description: Folder holding the database. Connect it to snpEff annotate.

params.label: Genome name
params.description: Names the database inside the folder. Use the same name in snpEff annotate.

params.label: Memory limit
params.description: For example 2g or 8g.

tools.command: mkdir -p {database}{genome_name} && cp {genome} {database}{genome_name}/sequences.fa && cp {annotation} {database}{genome_name}/genes.gtf && cfg=$(mktemp ./.snpeff_config.XXXXXX) && printf '%s.genome : %s\n' {genome_name} {genome_name} > "$cfg" && snpEff -Xmx{memory} -Duser.language=en -Duser.country=US build -gtf22 -noCheckCds -noCheckProtein -c "$cfg" -dataDir {database} {genome_name}; status=$?; rm -f "$cfg"; exit $status

tools.name: snpEff annotate
tools.description: Says what each variant does to the genes: missense, synonymous, intron, intergenic and so on.

inputs.name: vcf
inputs.label: Variants
inputs.description: A VCF file.

inputs.name: database
inputs.label: snpEff database folder
inputs.description: The folder that holds the genome's database: the output of snpEff build database, or a data folder from snpEff download.

outputs.name: annotated
outputs.label: Annotated variants
outputs.description: The VCF with an ANN field on every variant.

outputs.name: summary
outputs.label: Summary page
outputs.description: An HTML summary of the effects. MultiQC reads it.

outputs.name: stats
outputs.label: Effect counts
outputs.description: The same numbers as a CSV table.

params.label: Genome name
params.description: The name of the genome inside the database folder, as given when it was built.

params.label: Upstream and downstream distance
params.description: A variant this close before or after a gene is called upstream or downstream of it.

params.label: Leave out variants between genes
params.description: Skips the intergenic variants in the output.

params.label: Memory limit
params.description: For example 2g or 8g.

tools.command: cfg=$(mktemp ./.snpeff_config.XXXXXX) && printf '%s.genome : %s\n' {genome_name} {genome_name} > "$cfg" && snpEff -Xmx{memory} -Duser.language=en -Duser.country=US ann -c "$cfg" -dataDir {database} -ud {updown_distance} {no_intergenic} -stats {summary} -csvStats {stats} {genome_name} {vcf} > {annotated}; status=$?; rm -f "$cfg"; exit $status

needs_database.label: snpEff database
needs_database.hint: Build one for your own genome with the snpEff build database step, or download one with snpEff download (a human genome database is about 100 MB).

tools.name: Salmon quant
tools.description: Quantifies transcript abundance from single-end reads.

inputs.name: index
inputs.label: Salmon index
inputs.description: The folder made with Salmon index (connect it).

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Reads
inputs.description: Sequencing reads in FASTQ format (plain or .gz).

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Result folder
outputs.description: Salmon writes its results here.

outputs.name: quant
outputs.label: Abundances
outputs.description: The table of transcript abundances. It is always called quant.sf inside the result folder.

params.label: Library type
params.description: A detects the type automatically.

tools.name: featureCounts
tools.description: Counts reads per gene from alignments and an annotation.

inputs.name: bams
inputs.label: Alignments
inputs.description: One or more BAM or SAM files, counted into one table with one column per file. For paired-end reads tick Paired-end reads in Options.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.description: Gene annotation in GTF format.

outputs.name: counts
outputs.label: Count table
outputs.description: One row per gene, one column per input file.

outputs.name: summary
outputs.label: Counting summary
outputs.description: How many reads were assigned or not. MultiQC reads it. Always the count table's name plus .summary.

params.label: Library strandedness
params.description: Pick what your library kit makes. Most Illumina kits (TruSeq stranded, dUTP) are reverse-stranded. If unsure, run RSeQC infer experiment first. A wrong choice loses most reads.

option_labels.2: Reverse-stranded (dUTP kits: read 1 is the opposite strand)

params.label: Feature type
params.description: The GTF feature that reads are counted on.

params.label: Group by attribute
params.description: The GTF attribute that names each counted unit.

params.label: Paired-end reads
params.description: Count read pairs (fragments) instead of single reads. Tick this for paired-end data: featureCounts stops with an error when it finds pairs and this is off.

tools.name: HISAT2 build
tools.description: Builds the genome index HISAT2 needs to align RNA-seq reads.

inputs.name: genome
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The genome FASTA to index.

outputs.name: index_dir
outputs.label: Index folder
outputs.description: The HISAT2 index files. Connect it to HISAT2 as the genome index.

tools.name: Salmon index
tools.description: Builds the index Salmon quant needs from transcript sequences.

inputs.name: transcripts
inputs.label: Transcript sequences
inputs.description: One FASTA entry per transcript (cDNA). Make it from a genome and an annotation with gffread.

outputs.name: index_dir
outputs.label: Index folder
outputs.description: The Salmon index. Connect it to Salmon quant.

params.label: Word size (k-mer)
params.description: Odd number. 31 suits reads of 75 bases or longer; use about 21 for shorter reads.

tools.name: STAR genome index
tools.description: Builds the genome index STAR needs to align RNA-seq reads, with the known splice junctions of an annotation.

inputs.name: genome
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The genome FASTA to index.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.description: Optional but recommended: STAR then knows the splice junctions of your genes. GTF format.

outputs.name: index_dir
outputs.label: Index folder
outputs.description: The STAR index. Connect it to STAR as the genome index.

params.label: Splice junction overhang
params.description: Read length minus 1. 100 suits reads up to 101 bases. Only used when a gene annotation is given.

params.label: Index size setting
params.description: 14 suits a human or mouse genome. For a small genome use about log2(genome size) / 2 - 1 (a 5 million base genome: 10).

tools.name: kallisto index
tools.description: Builds the index kallisto quant needs from transcript sequences.

inputs.name: transcripts
inputs.label: Transcript sequences
inputs.description: One FASTA entry per transcript (cDNA). Make it from a genome and an annotation with gffread.

outputs.name: index
outputs.label: Index file
outputs.description: The kallisto index. Connect it to kallisto quant.

params.label: Word size (k-mer)
params.description: Odd number up to 31. Use a smaller value (about 21) for reads shorter than 50 bases.

tools.name: gffread transcripts
tools.description: Cuts the transcript sequences (exons joined together) out of a genome using an annotation.

inputs.name: genome
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The genome FASTA the annotation belongs to. gffread also writes a .fai index file next to it.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.description: Gene annotation in GTF or GFF3 format.

outputs.name: transcripts
outputs.label: Transcript sequences
outputs.description: One FASTA entry per transcript. Connect it to Salmon index or kallisto index.

tools.name: Annotation to BED12
tools.description: Converts a gene annotation (GTF or GFF3) to the BED12 gene model that RSeQC reads.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.description: Gene annotation in GTF or GFF3 format.

outputs.name: bed
outputs.label: Gene model (BED12)
outputs.description: One line per transcript with its exon blocks. Connect it to the RSeQC steps.

tools.name: HISAT2
tools.description: Splice-aware RNA-seq aligner, single-end or paired-end. Writes SAM.

inputs.name: index
inputs.label: Genome index folder
inputs.description: The folder made with HISAT2 build (connect it).

inputs.name: reads1
inputs.label: Reads (first of the pair)
inputs.description: FASTQ with the reads, or the first file of a pair.

inputs.name: reads2
inputs.label: Reads (second of the pair)
inputs.description: Leave empty for single-end reads.

outputs.name: sam
outputs.label: Alignments
outputs.description: The alignments in SAM format. Sort them with samtools sort next.

outputs.name: summary
outputs.label: Alignment summary
outputs.description: How many reads aligned. MultiQC reads it.

params.label: Prepare for StringTie
params.description: Tick this when the alignments go to StringTie to assemble transcripts.

params.label: Longest intron
params.description: Introns longer than this many bases are not searched for. The default suits most animals; lower it for yeast or plants.

tools.command: set -- -U {reads1}; if [ -n "{reads2}" ]; then set -- -1 {reads1} -2 {reads2}; fi; hisat2 -p {threads} {dta} --max-intronlen {max_intron} -x {index}/genome "$@" -S {sam} --new-summary --summary-file {summary}

tools.name: kallisto quant
tools.description: Quantifies transcript abundance from single-end or paired-end reads, without aligning them.

inputs.name: index
inputs.label: kallisto index
inputs.description: The index made with kallisto index (connect it).

inputs.name: reads1
inputs.label: Reads (first of the pair)
inputs.description: FASTQ with the reads, or the first file of a pair.

inputs.name: reads2
inputs.label: Reads (second of the pair)
inputs.description: Leave empty for single-end reads. kallisto then needs the fragment length from Options.

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Result folder
outputs.description: kallisto writes its results here.

outputs.name: abundance
outputs.label: Abundances
outputs.description: The table of transcript abundances. It is always called abundance.tsv inside the result folder.

outputs.name: log
outputs.label: Run log
outputs.description: kallisto's progress messages. MultiQC reads it.

params.label: Average fragment length
params.description: Only used for single-end reads (when the second reads file is empty): the average length of the sequenced DNA fragments, from your library preparation.

params.label: Fragment length spread
params.description: Only used for single-end reads: the standard deviation of the fragment length.

params.label: Library strandedness
params.description: Pick what your library kit makes. Most Illumina kits (TruSeq stranded, dUTP) are reverse-stranded. If unsure, run RSeQC infer experiment on an alignment.

option_labels.--rf-stranded: Reverse-stranded (dUTP kits: read 1 is the opposite strand)

params.label: Bootstrap samples
params.description: Repeats of the estimate that show how certain it is. Needed only to compare samples with sleuth; 0 is fastest.

tools.command: set -- --single -l {fragment_length} -s {fragment_sd}; if [ -n "{reads2}" ]; then set --; fi; kallisto quant -i {index} -o {out_dir} -t {threads} "$@" {strand} -b {bootstrap_samples} {reads1} {reads2} 2> {log} || (cat {log} >&2; false)

tools.name: StringTie assemble
tools.description: Assembles transcripts from RNA-seq alignments, optionally guided by a gene annotation, and estimates their abundance.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM sorted by genome position. Made with HISAT2 (tick Prepare for StringTie) and samtools sort.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Guide annotation
inputs.description: Optional. With an annotation StringTie also finds the known genes; without one it assembles from the reads alone.

outputs.name: gtf
outputs.label: Assembled transcripts
outputs.description: The transcripts StringTie found, with their coverage and TPM. GTF format.

outputs.name: genes
outputs.label: Gene abundances
outputs.description: One row per gene with coverage, FPKM and TPM.

params.label: Library strandedness
params.description: Pick what your library kit makes. Most Illumina kits (TruSeq stranded, dUTP) are reverse-stranded. If unsure, run RSeQC infer experiment on an alignment.

option_labels.--rf: Reverse-stranded (dUTP kits: read 1 is the opposite strand)

params.label: Minimum coverage
params.description: Transcripts covered by fewer reads on average than this are dropped.

params.label: Minimum isoform fraction
params.description: Transcripts of a gene with less than this share of the gene's reads are dropped (0 to 1).

tools.name: StringTie quantify
tools.description: Measures the abundance of the transcripts of an annotation (no new transcripts are made).

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM sorted by genome position.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.description: The transcripts to measure: a GTF or GFF3 file, or the assembled transcripts of StringTie assemble.

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Result folder
outputs.description: StringTie writes its tables here, including the .ctab files Ballgown reads.

outputs.name: transcripts
outputs.label: Transcript abundances
outputs.description: The annotated transcripts with coverage, FPKM and TPM. Always called transcripts.gtf inside the result folder.

outputs.name: genes
outputs.label: Gene abundances
outputs.description: One row per gene. Always called gene_abundances.tsv inside the result folder.

params.label: Library strandedness
params.description: Pick what your library kit makes. Most Illumina kits (TruSeq stranded, dUTP) are reverse-stranded. If unsure, run RSeQC infer experiment on an alignment.

option_labels.--rf: Reverse-stranded (dUTP kits: read 1 is the opposite strand)

tools.name: RSeQC infer experiment
tools.description: Works out whether an RNA-seq library is stranded, and which way, from where reads fall on genes.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM of RNA-seq reads aligned to the genome.

inputs.name: gene_model
inputs.label: Gene model (BED12)
inputs.description: The genes in BED12 format. Make it from a GTF with Annotation to BED12.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Strandedness report
outputs.description: The share of reads that follow each strand rule. MultiQC reads it.

params.label: Reads to check
params.description: The first this many reads that fall on genes are checked. More is slower and barely changes the answer.

params.label: Minimum mapping quality
params.description: Reads below this mapping quality are skipped.

tools.name: RSeQC read distribution
tools.description: Shows how the reads divide between exons, introns and the regions around genes.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM of RNA-seq reads aligned to the genome.

inputs.name: gene_model
inputs.label: Gene model (BED12)
inputs.description: The genes in BED12 format. Make it from a GTF with Annotation to BED12.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Distribution report
outputs.description: Bases and read tags per region type. MultiQC reads it.
